CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.error: Thinks being special means being better than other people.

example.question: What does it mean that you are God's special creation?
example.wrong_answer: You are better than other children
example.correct_answer: God made you with love and no one else is exactly like you

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.cause: The word special is heard as a prize or a rank.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.reveals: Offer "You are better than other children" beside "God made you with love and no one else is exactly like you" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.help: Say that every child is special in the same way, and ask each child to name one thing that makes a classmate special.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.feedback: Everyone is God's special creation. Being special does not make you better than others, because God made them with love too.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

review.mark: plausible, to confirm by a teacher
review.note: Own judgement: believable for a Kenyan child of this age, but we have no source or homework count. A teacher who knows the class should say whether children really hold it.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.error: Thinks a person is a chance event, without a plan or a maker.

example.question: According to Psalm 139:13-14, how did God make you?

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.help: Read Psalm 139:13-14 slowly and ask who is doing the knitting.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.feedback: Psalm 139:13-14 says that God formed each person and that we are fearfully and wonderfully made. You were not made by chance.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.error: Thinks God made only the first people, Adam and Eve, not each person today.

example.question: Who made you, according to the Bible?
example.wrong_answer: God made only the first man and woman, and I came from my parents only
example.correct_answer: God, who made every person in his image

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.cause: The creation story is told as a story of long ago only.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.reveals: Offer "God made only the first man and woman, and I came from my parents only" beside "God, who made every person in his image" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.help: Link Genesis 1:27 ("God created mankind in his own image") to Psalm 139:13 about each person.
CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.UNIQUE_CRE.feedback: Genesis 1:27 says God made human beings in his image, and Psalm 139:13 says he formed each of us. God is the maker of every person, including you.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.error: Thinks that feeling angry is itself a sin.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.feedback: Ephesians 4:26 says "in your anger do not sin". Anger is a feeling that comes to everyone. The wrong is in what we do with it.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.error: Thinks you should keep anger inside until you can get even.

example.question: What should you do about anger, according to Ephesians 4:26?
example.wrong_answer: Keep it and pay the person back later
example.correct_answer: Settle it before the sun goes down

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.feedback: Ephesians 4:26 says do not let the sun go down while you are still angry. Settle it quickly by forgiving or talking, not by planning to pay back.

review.note: Own judgement: believable for a Kenyan child of this age, but we have no source or homework count. A teacher who knows the class should say whether children really hold it.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.FEELINGS.M.error: Thinks we rejoice only when everything is going well.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.feedback: A right choice is guided by the word of God, not by what the group does. Choose to obey and attend, even when friends choose differently.

CRES.G4.CREATI.SELF_AWARENESS.CHOICES.M_.feedback: We make many choices every day: what to say, whom to sit with, whether to obey. Small choices matter too.

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks honouring parents is only for when they give us things or agree with us.

example.wrong_answer: Only when they give me what I want

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks a child must keep a secret when an adult asks for it.

example.question: An adult touches you in a way that feels wrong and says "keep it a secret". What should you do?
example.wrong_answer: Keep the secret so I do not get in trouble
example.correct_answer: Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: The child fears trouble or is told to be quiet.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Keep the secret so I do not get in trouble" beside "Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Say clearly: a secret about touching is never to be kept. Practise telling a teacher or parent.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: A wrong touch is never a secret to keep. Say NO, go away and tell a trusted adult, such as a parent or teacher, or call Childline Kenya on 116.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks only strangers can hurt a child and that people we know are always safe.

example.question: Who might touch a child in a wrong way?
example.correct_answer: Anyone, so a child must know what is not allowed and tell

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: Warnings about strangers hide that harm can come from known people.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..reveals: Offer "Only strangers" beside "Anyone, so a child must know what is not allowed and tell" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Teach the rule: private parts are private, whoever asks.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: Anyone can do wrong, even a person we know. The rule is that private parts are private. If anyone breaks it, say NO and tell a trusted adult.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

review.mark: common in the literature
review.source: Finkelhor (1984), Child Sexual Abuse: New Theory and Research: most harm to children comes from people they know, so "stranger danger" alone is a misleading rule.

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..error: Thinks it is the child's fault if he or she is touched wrongly, so there is no need to tell.

example.question: A child was touched wrongly. Whose fault is it?
example.wrong_answer: The child's fault, so she should say nothing
example.correct_answer: Never the child's fault, and she should tell

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..cause: Shame and fear stop a child from telling.

CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..help: Say it slowly: it is never your fault. Name the adults who will believe and help.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..feedback: It is never the child's fault. The person who touched wrongly did wrong. Tell a trusted adult, and keep telling until someone helps.
CRES.G4.CREATI.MY_FAMILY_FAMILY_MEMBERS..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

review.mark: common in the literature
review.source: Summit (1983), Child Abuse and Neglect 7: children commonly blame themselves, feel shame and delay or avoid telling.
